title: introduce-runway-metrics-and-invocation-trace-debouncer
author: Aisha Khan
release_notes: Adds per-tenant runway metric, invocation trace debouncer, new dashboard panels, and tuned alerts to reduce transient alert noise and improve cost forecasting.
commits: a1b2c3d: add runway metric producer and tenant sampling hook
d4e5f6g: introduce trace debouncer middleware and unit tests
h7i8j9k: console: dashboard tiles for runway and debouncer stats
l0m1n2o: observability: alert rule adjustments and doc updates
p3q4r5s: integration tests and CI flake fixes
body:
Motivation: Production customers see repeated short-lived token bursts that trigger costly paging and noisy SRE alerts. The platform lacks a concise early-warning signal for per-tenant cost runway (how many tokens at current burnrate before a spike) and a lightweight suppression mechanism that reduces alert churn for sub-second invocation bursts. This change introduces a per-tenant "runway" metric that projects remaining token budget at current burn rate, plus an invocation trace debouncer that groups short-lived invocations into a single representative trace for alerting and dashboards.

What this PR does: 1) Adds a new timeseries metric telemetry.runway.tokens_per_tenant (gauge + derivative) computed from per-tenant token burn and quota metadata. The metric is coarse by default (1m rollup) and has an opt-in high-resolution path for Dedicated customers. 2) Implements an invocation trace debouncer middleware in the runtime tracer: invocations shorter than 300ms are coalesced for span sampling and alert evaluation into a single debounced span per tenant per-second window. Debounced spans carry aggregated token counts and a stability score. 3) Console: new dashboard tiles in Observability -> Cost that show per-tenant runway heatmap, runway-to-alert mapping, and debouncer hit-rate. 4) Alerting: new alert rule runway.low (< 10% runway for 5m) with adaptive suppression for debounced bursts, and tuned alert labels so on-call can see whether an alert came from a debounced aggregate or a canonical long invocation. 5) Documentation: adds telemetry and alerting guide section and a migration note for Dedicated customers that want high-resolution runway.

Checklist: - [x] Add metric producer and runtime hook - [x] Add debouncer middleware and tests - [x] Add dashboard tiles and example queries - [x] Add alert rule and unit/integration tests - [x] Update docs and changelog - [x] Run CI and fix flakes

Files changed (high level): - telemetry/metrics/producer/tenant_runway.go: new logic to compute runway projection with outlier-resistant smoothing - tracing/middleware/debouncer.go: debouncer implementation and configuration knobs - console/dashboard/cost_runway.json: dashboard layout and queries - alerting/rules/runway_low.yaml: new alert rule with suppression annotations - docs/observability/runway.md: user-facing docs and examples - tests/*: unit and integration tests covering projection math and debouncer semantics - ci/integration.yml: add a quick telemetry smoke test to the pipeline

Summary of commits: a1b2c3d adds the initial telemetry producer and hook into token counter; d4e5f6g adds debouncer with deterministic unit tests; h7i8j9k wires up dashboard tiles and example queries in the console; l0m1n2o adds alert rule and docs; p3q4r5s fixes CI timing flakiness discovered during runs.

Design notes and choices: - Runway projection uses an exponential smoothing on burnrate with a capped lookback to avoid overreacting to short bursts. We expose both absolute runway (tokens) and normalized runway_pct for policy decisions. - Debouncer is intentionally conservative: it does not drop traces, only synthesizes an aggregated dep-span used for alerting and dashboard signals. Raw invocation logs remain available for debugging. - For Dedicated customers we provide a config flag telemetry.runway.high_res=true to enable 5s resolution; default stays at 60s to control cardinality. - Alert suppression uses a short grace period (1m) for debounced aggregates to avoid duplicate alerts from rapid flapping; suppression is annotated in the alert payload so automated runbooks can behave differently.

Review conversation highlights: - Claire: "Can we ensure runway calc accounts for reserved token buckets?" -> Aisha: "Yes, runway uses tenant.quota and respects reserved buckets; added unit tests for that scenario (see a1b2c3d)." - Miguel: "Debouncer might hide important micro-failures; what's the rollback plan?" -> Aisha: "Debouncer is opt-out per-tenant via telemetry.tracing.debounce=false and we included an operator gauge debouncer.hit_rate to make it observable; removed any automatic suppression for errors > 5% within the debounced window." - Samir: "Dashboard queries look heavy at 5s resolution." -> Aisha: "Default dashboards use 1m rollups; high-res is behind a toggle and shows a warning."

CI and testing: Initial run showed a flaky integration on the telemetry smoke test (timeout on CI runner). I increased the test timeout, made a deterministic seed for the debouncer unit test, and re-ran; final CI status: all checks passing (unit, integration, lint).

Merge outcome: Merged via squash merge on 2026-02-20 after approvals from Claire and Miguel and a +1 from Samir. Post-merge: feature gated for all tenants; Dedicated customers can enable high-res via Console -> Account -> Telemetry toggles.

Follow-ups planned (ENG backlog): - ENG-4400: expose runway forecasts in billing export and infra cost predictions - ENG-4401: automated remediation playbook to throttle non-critical tenants when runway < 5% - PM-211: customer-facing changelog and opt-in email for Dedicated customers

Notes for oncall: new alert labels include run_type:debounced|canonical and runway_pct; use these to quickly determine if noise suppression masked transient bursts. If investigating a runway.low alert, consult the debouncer.hit_rate and the per-tenant token histogram to see if the signal is persistent or bursty.
